items.title: How to Stop Complaining About Your Software
items.summary: Julie Zhuo argues that AI is enabling an era of hyperpersonalized software — where people build tools fitted to their exact workflow rather than tolerating generic apps — and illustrates it by building a Duolingo-style math and reading app for her own kids, populated with their friends' names and hobbies.
items.why: Her homemade kids' learning app is essentially a proof of concept for what Cuemath's practice app could become: problems and stories built around each student's own world, making the content feel made for them rather than at them.

items.title: Large Scale Agent Coordination
items.summary: Luke Wroblewski examines how multi-agent AI systems coordinate complex work at scale — through isolated workspaces, specialized agent roles, and intelligent handoffs — using the developer platform Intent as a concrete case study for running thousands of agents across distributed devices.
items.why: When Cuemath evaluates adding AI tutoring or practice features, this is the practitioner framework for understanding what 'multiple AI agents working together' actually looks like in a product — Wroblewski writes from shipping, not from theory.

items.title: Why Product Sense is the only product skill that will matter in the AI age
items.summary: Shreyas Doshi argues that as AI tools become universally available and roughly equivalent in power, they stop being a competitive edge — the only sustainable differentiator becomes Product Sense: the human judgment (empathy, taste, simulation, strategic thinking) you bring on top of what the AI gives you.
items.why: This is the clearest articulation of why design and product judgment matter more, not less, as Cuemath ships AI-assisted features — the case that Manik's role isn't being automated, it's becoming the whole point.

items.title: Raw and unrefined: Studio Tyrrell's identity for Manta Chocolate leans into the tension between purity and pleasure
items.summary: Studio Tyrrell built an identity for a plant-based chocolate brand that makes strict ingredient transparency feel sensory and indulgent rather than clinical — ingredients are displayed boldly up front, and a deliberately handmade logotype breaks the system's rigor to introduce warmth and tension.
items.why: The design challenge here — making something ascetic and disciplined also feel rich and desirable — maps directly onto the Cuemath problem: how do you make serious math practice feel inviting rather than medicinal.

items.title: Le Phénix Scène Nationale Valenciennes, 2026–27 season
items.summary: Studio Paul Andali's seasonal identity for a French national theater, built around BBB Poppins TN — a gender-inclusive typeface variant from the Bye Bye Binary foundry — applied across posters, programs, signage, and digital assets with animated type and chromatic distortion.
items.why: Choosing BBB Poppins TN as the identity backbone isn't a typeface pick, it's a values decision made visible — this is what a design system embedding organizational values in every touchpoint looks like in practice, a question live for CueDesign as it matures.
